answer: A staking bond makes each identity expensive to fake: to join, an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if peers catch it voting twice or copying others. Like an opal that only reveals its fire under light, the bond proves its value only when the agent behaves honestly over time. Newcomers start on a small knoll of trust, earning a lantern of reputation by completing verified work before they can vote on larger decisions. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds and risk losing them all, so the cost of a sybil swarm quickly exceeds any reward it could steal.
